claim_text: Microsoft reported quarterly revenue of $81.3 billion.
quote: This quarter, revenue was $81.3 billion, up 17% and 15% in constant currency.
speaker: AMY HOOD

claim_text: Microsoft reported adjusted earnings per share of $4.14.
quote: Earnings per share was $4.14, an increase of 24 and 21% in constant currency, when adjusted for the impact from our investment in OpenAI.
speaker: AMY HOOD

claim_text: Company gross margin was 68% and declined slightly year over year.
quote: Company gross margin percentage was 68%, down slightly year-over-year primarily driven by continued investments in AI infrastructure and growing AI product usage that was partially offset by ongoing efficiency gains, particularly in Azure and M365 Commercial cloud, as well as sales mix shift to higher margin businesses.
speaker: AMY HOOD

claim_text: Microsoft Cloud revenue was $51.5 billion.
quote: Microsoft Cloud revenue was $51.5 billion and grew 26% and 24% in constant currency.
speaker: AMY HOOD

claim_text: Intelligent Cloud revenue was $32.9 billion and grew 29% year over year.
quote: Revenue was $32.9 billion and grew 29% and 28% in constant currency.
speaker: AMY HOOD

claim_text: Azure and other cloud services revenue grew 39% year over year and 38% in constant currency.
quote: In Azure and other cloud services, revenue grew 39% and 38% in constant currency, slightly ahead of expectations, with ongoing efficiency gains across our fungible fleet enabling us to reallocate some capacity to Azure that was monetized in the quarter.
speaker: AMY HOOD

claim_text: More Personal Computing revenue was $14.3 billion and declined 3% year over year.
quote: Revenue was $14.3 billion and declined 3%.
speaker: AMY HOOD

claim_text: Microsoft added nearly one gigawatt of total capacity during the quarter.
quote: All up, we added nearly one gigawatt of total capacity this quarter alone.
speaker: SATYA NADELLA

claim_text: Microsoft had 15 million paid Microsoft 365 Copilot seats after record quarterly seat additions.
quote: All up, it was a record quarter for Microsoft 365 Copilot seat adds, up over 160% year-over-year. We saw accelerating seat growth quarter-over-quarter and now have 15 million paid Microsoft 365 Copilot seats, and multiples more enterprise Chat users.
speaker: SATYA NADELLA

claim_text: GitHub Copilot had more than 4.7 million paid subscribers.
quote: And, all up now we have over 4.7 million paid Copilot subscribers, up 75% year-over-year.
speaker: SATYA NADELLA

claim_text: Management said customer demand continued to exceed available supply.
quote: Our customer demand continues to exceed our supply.
speaker: AMY HOOD

claim_text: Commercial remaining performance obligation was $625 billion, up 110% year over year, with a weighted average duration of about 2.5 years.
quote: Commercial remaining performance obligation, which continues to be reported net of reserves, increased to $625 billion and was up 110% year-over-year with a weighted average duration of approximately two and a half years.
speaker: AMY HOOD

claim_text: About 45% of commercial remaining performance obligation came from OpenAI.
quote: Approximately 45% of our commercial RPO balance is from OpenAI.
speaker: AMY HOOD

claim_text: Capital expenditure was $37.5 billion, with roughly two thirds spent on short-lived assets, mainly graphics and central processing units.
quote: Capital expenditures were $37.5 billion, and this quarter, roughly two thirds of our capex was on short-lived assets, primarily GPUs and CPUs.
speaker: AMY HOOD

claim_text: Cash flow from operations was $35.8 billion and free cash flow was $5.9 billion.
quote: Cash flow from operations was $35.8 billion, up 60% driven by strong cloud billings and collections. And free cash flow was $5.9 billion and decreased sequentially reflecting the higher cash capital expenditures from a lower mix of finance leases.
speaker: AMY HOOD

claim_text: Microsoft guided next-quarter revenue to $80.65 billion to $81.75 billion.
quote: We expect revenue of $80.65 to $81.75 billion or growth of 15% to %17 with continued strong growth across our commercial businesses, partially offset by our consumer businesses.
speaker: AMY HOOD

claim_text: Microsoft guided next-quarter Intelligent Cloud revenue to $34.1 billion to $34.4 billion.
quote: For Intelligent Cloud, we expect revenue of $34.1 to $34.4 billion, or growth of 27% to 29%.
speaker: AMY HOOD

claim_text: Microsoft expected next-quarter Azure revenue growth of 37% to 38% in constant currency.
quote: In Azure, we expect Q3 revenue growth to be between 37% and 38% in constant currency against a prior year comparable that included significantly accelerating growth rates in both Q3 and Q4.
speaker: AMY HOOD

claim_text: Microsoft expected cloud gross margin of roughly 65% next quarter.
quote: Microsoft Cloud gross margin percentage should be roughly 65%, down year-over-year driven by continued investments in AI.
speaker: AMY HOOD

claim_text: Management raised its fiscal-year operating-margin expectation to a slight year-over-year increase.
quote: With the strong work delivered in H1 to prioritize investment in key growth areas and the favorable impact from a higher mix of revenue in our Windows OEM and Commercial on-prem businesses, we now expect FY26 operating margins to be up slightly.
speaker: AMY HOOD

claim_text: Management attributed the lower company gross margin mainly to artificial-intelligence infrastructure investment and growing usage, partly offset by efficiency gains and business mix.
quote: Company gross margin percentage was 68%, down slightly year-over-year primarily driven by continued investments in AI infrastructure and growing AI product usage that was partially offset by ongoing efficiency gains, particularly in Azure and M365 Commercial cloud, as well as sales mix shift to higher margin businesses.
speaker: AMY HOOD

claim_text: Management said Azure guidance should be viewed as an allocated-capacity guide because compute is also assigned to first-party products and research and development.
quote: Sometimes, I think it’s probably better to think about the Azure guidance that we give as an allocated capacity guide about what we can deliver in Azure revenue, because as we spend the capital and put GPUs, specifically, it applies to CPUs, but GPUs more specifically, we’re really making long-term decisions.
speaker: AMY HOOD

claim_text: Management said many graphics-processing-unit contracts cover the hardware's entire useful life, reducing the residual demand risk.
quote: And on the GPU contracts that we’ve talked about, including for some of our largest customers, those are sold for the entire useful life of the GPU.
speaker: AMY HOOD

claim_text: Management said roughly $350 billion, or 55%, of commercial remaining performance obligation related to the broader portfolio rather than OpenAI and had grown 28%.
quote: The first thing to focus on is the reason we talked about that number is because 55%, or roughly $350 billion, is related to the breadth of our portfolio, a breadth of customers across solutions, across Azure, across industries, across geographies.
speaker: AMY HOOD

claim_text: The timing of capacity delivery and contract mix could make Azure growth vary from quarter to quarter.
quote: As a reminder, there can be quarterly variability in year-on-year growth rates depending on the timing of capacity delivery and when it comes online, as well as from in-period revenue recognition depending on the mix of contracts.
speaker: AMY HOOD

claim_text: Rising memory prices could increase capital expenditure and would affect cloud gross margin gradually as assets depreciate over six years.
quote: In addition, rising memory prices would impact capital expenditures, though the impact on Microsoft Cloud gross margins will build more gradually as these assets depreciate over six years.
speaker: AMY HOOD

claim_text: Oracle reported fiscal second-quarter cloud infrastructure revenue of $4.1 billion, up 68% year over year.
quote: Q2 Cloud Infrastructure (IaaS) Revenue $4.1 billion, up 68% in USD and up 66% in constant currency
speaker: Oracle
